# dsh-relay-reasoning
English | 中文
Real reasoning levels — **off / low / medium / high / max** — on every model of your OpenAI-compatib
le relay, right in the DSH model picker.
## The problem
Relays such as a self-hosted gateway fronting many models accept the `reasoning_effort` request para
meter, but DSH offers no reasoning control for them. The reason is structural: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm
-pi-ai` only publishes selectable levels for a model whose `reasoningEfforts` field declares them, s
o a route configured by hand shows nothing.
Declaring those levels by hand means repeating seven lines for every model — and re-doing it wheneve
r the model list changes.
## What this plugin does
It writes `reasoningEfforts` into the `llm-pi-ai` profile entry for every model on the configured pr
oviders, and the picker immediately offers those levels. No restart, and no editing of your model li
ders, and the picker immediately offers those levels. No restart, and no editing of your model list.
**It keeps up with your configuration.** The first pass runs at activation, and every later profile
configuration reload — adding a relay or a model from the settings UI, editing a route — runs it aga
in and fills in whatever is missing. A relay you connect while DSH is running gets its levels withou
in whatever is missing. A relay you connect while DSH is running gets its levels without a restart.
## Why these five levels
pi-ai understands seven levels, but a relay does not distinguish all of them. Measured over three pr
ompts and two passes on one relay route, median reasoning tokens per level:
| Level | median reasoning tokens |

| off | 0 |
| minimal | 108 |
| low | 122 |
| medium | 155 |
| high | 142 |
| xhigh | 125 |
| max |

| 0 |
| minimal | 108 |
| low | 122 |
| medium | 155 |
| high | 142 |
| xhigh | 125 |
| max | 359 |
`max` is roughly double every other level, so it is a genuinely stronger tier and is included by def
is roughly double every other level, so it is a genuinely stronger tier and is included by default.
The five middle levels (`minimal` through `xhigh`) land within each other's noise on this route, so
publishing them would only duplicate choices. They stay out by default but can be requested through
`levels` if a route of yours does distinguish them.
If your relay turns out to ignore `max`, drop it with `levels: [off, low, medium, high]` so the pick
er does not offer a level that does nothing.

## Configuration
The plugin row takes an optional config:

`providers: []` means the plugin covers every provider on the entry, so adding a new relay needs no
` means the plugin covers every provider on the entry, so adding a new relay needs no plugin change.
`levels` defaults to `off, low, medium, high, max`. Narrow it if your relay ignores a level:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Any subset of `off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max` is accepted; names are published in asce
nding order and unknown names are dropped.
## Idempotent
A pass writes nothing when every model already declares exactly the configured levels; it inspects a
nd stops. Updating the package, and the configuration reload caused by the plugin's own write, there
fore never churn your configuration, and any leftover declaration from a manual setup is detected an
hurn your configuration, and any leftover declaration from a manual setup is detected and rewritten.
Changing `levels` does rewrite the affected models, because their current declaration no longer matc
ging `levels` does rewrite the affected models, because their current declaration no longer matches.
`force: true` is honoured at activation only — it rewrites once, including declarations that are alr
eady correct. Later reloads ignore it, because honouring it every time would rewrite the same declar
ation and reload in a loop.
## How it works
Three details are worth knowing if you read the source.
**It does not override the `llm-pi-ai` row.** A Cordis loader patch replaces a row's `config` wholes
ale rather than merging it, so a patch that added `reasoningEfforts` would erase `baseURL`, the cred
ential reference, and the whole model list. The plugin instead calls `settings.mutate()` with path-s
coped operations, touching only `providers.<name>.models[i].reasoningEfforts`.
**It writes outside the transaction.** The HMR config editor refuses to nest transactions, and its g
uard reads an `AsyncLocalStorage` store that survives awaits and timers, so deferring is not enough.
The plugin runs the write through `hmr.executing.exit()` — the same mechanism `dsh-hmr` uses when w
iring a config watcher from inside a transaction.
**It listens to `app-boot/config-reload`.** Every successful profile reload emits that event — inclu
ding a relay added from the settings UI. The plugin inspects once shortly afterwards; a reload cause
d by its own write only finds everything already correct and stops, so there is no loop, and a burst
of events collapses into one inspection.
## Compatibility

- Requires DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.1`.
- No runtime dependencies: only `node:fs` and Host-provided services.
- Works with any OpenAI-compatible route declared on the `llm-pi-ai` entry, not just one relay.
